mainTopic: End of פרק הזורק (the relative in a גט מקושר and קיום from any three), and the start of פרק המגרש: a גט that frees the woman to marry anyone 'except so-and-so'
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the empty spot in a גט מקושר may be filled by a relative only when one witness is missing. אביי then learns two things from the fact that no fixed spot was set for that relative. First, he may sign first, in the middle, or last. Second, the גט can be confirmed from any three witnesses, even if they did not sign in a row. רבי אמי rules in practice that a missing witness may be completed even with a slave from the marketplace, and פרק הזורק ends. The new chapter's משנה brings a husband who frees his wife to marry anyone 'אלא' one man: רבי אליעזר says the divorce works and חכמים say it does not. The משנה adds that the fix is to give the גט again with a full release, but a written exception ruins the גט even if it is erased. The גמרא asks whether אלא means 'except' or 'on condition', and רבינא proves from a משנה about נגעים that it means 'except'. The amud ends by quoting רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says everyone agrees 'except' fails and places the argument on a condition instead. His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The list goes one by one, so only one witness may be missing
steps.stepSummary: The proof from before is completed: the teaching lists cases where only one witness is missing each time, so the rule only covers one missing witness. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it skips along and teaches each case with one missing; learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof that started earlier and accepts it with the words שמע מינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases like seven ties with six witnesses, always only one witness short. It never lists a case two short. So the leniency of a קרח, an empty spot filled by a relative, applies only to one missing witness.

keyTerms.meaning: skips along, jumps from case to case
one by one, one at a time
learn from it, so it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The empty spot in a גט מקושר is allowed only when one witness is missing, never two.

phrases.english: as it skips along and teaches one by one;
phrases.notes: Every case on the list has just one witness fewer than the ties, like seven ties and six witnesses.

phrases.english: conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָא מְדַלֵּג וְתָנֵי חַד חַד שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קרח leniency applies only to one missing witness.

steps.title: The relative may sign anywhere on the document
steps.stepSummary: אביי learns that the relative who fills the empty spot may sign first, in the middle, or last, as he wishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from it that this relative signs wherever he wants, at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a new practical rule about where the relative may place his signature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this we knew a relative may fill the one empty spot. אביי adds a new detail: his spot is not fixed. He may be first, middle, or last among the witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: a relative, normally not fit to be a witness
signs
if he wants

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from it,
this relative signs if he wants
phrases.notes: This is the relative who is allowed to fill the one empty spot in a tied גט.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּתְּחִילָּה, בֵּין בָּאֶמְצַע, בֵּין בַּסּוֹף.
phrases.english: either at the beginning, or in the middle, or at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new inference on top of the קרח teaching just confirmed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The relative in a גט מקושר may sign in any position.

steps.title: How does אביי know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source shows that the relative may sign anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of אביי's rule. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's rule was stated without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what in the teaching shows the relative's spot is open.

keyTerms.meaning: from where? what is the source?

phrases.english: From where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of אביי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing the relative may sign in any position.

steps.title: No fixed spot was given to him
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the teaching never set a particular place for the relative, so any place is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that it did not set a place for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is the silence of the teaching: it never named a spot for the relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the relative had to sign in a certain position, the teaching would have said so. Since it gave no position, any position is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: fixed, set
a place, a position

phrases.english: From the fact that it did not set a place for him.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No fixed place was set for the relative, so he may sign anywhere.

steps.title: Any three witnesses can confirm the גט
steps.stepSummary: אביי draws a second lesson: a גט מקושר can be confirmed from any three of its witnesses, and they do not have to be signed one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And learn from it: we confirm the גט from any three, and we do not need them to be in a row.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second rule learned from the same fact: confirming the גט does not need three witnesses in a row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיום means checking the signatures to confirm the גט. אביי says any three witnesses on the גט are enough, even if they are spread out, such as the first, fourth, and sixth. This rule is proven in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: we confirm, we validate the signatures (קיום)
three
in a row, one right after the other

steps.confusionAlert: Here רצופין means witnesses signed next to each other in a row. It is not about time.

phrases.english: And learn from it:
from any three we confirm the document,
and we do not need them to be in a row.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second inference from the same fact that no place was set for the relative.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט מקושר can be confirmed from any three witnesses, even if they are not signed in a row.

steps.title: If three in a row were needed, many relatives could have been allowed
steps.stepSummary: The proof: if only three in a row counted, the relative could have been given a fixed spot, and חז"ל could have allowed many relatives. Since they allowed only one, any three must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think we need them in a row, they should have set a place for this relative, at the beginning, the middle, or the end, and then allowed many relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that any three may be used by showing what would follow if three in a row were required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only three in a row counted, relatives could be placed in fixed spots so every row of three always has two kosher witnesses. Then many relatives would be fine. Since only one relative is allowed, any three may be picked, and that could land on two relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: if you would think
let them allow, declare kosher
many, a lot

steps.whatToRemember: Only one relative is allowed because a גט מקושר can be confirmed from any three witnesses. If those three included two relatives, the confirmation would not be valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the reason behind the limit of one relative: the way קיום works is what keeps the number of relatives at one.

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that we need them in a row,
let them set a place for this relative,
at the beginning, or in the middle, or at the end;
and let them allow many of them.
phrases.notes: He means many relatives, placed so that every three in a row still has two kosher witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the rule of step 5 by showing what would follow from the opposite view.
steps.raayaObject: That any three witnesses may be used for קיום, not only three in a row.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that only one relative is allowed and no fixed place is set for him. If three in a row were required, many relatives in fixed places could have been allowed.

steps.title: רבי אמי rules: complete the missing witness even with a slave
steps.stepSummary: A practical case came before רבי אמי, and he ruled that the missing witness spot may be filled even by a slave from the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they came before רבי אמי, he said: Go out and complete it with a slave from the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life case to show how the הלכה was decided about filling the missing witness spot on a גט. This closes the discussion of the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps talked about who may fill an empty witness spot on a גט. Here רבי אמי rules leniently: even a slave picked from the street is good enough to complete it. This follows the view of בן ננס in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gave the practical ruling here
Complete or fill in (the missing witness)
A slave
Marketplace; here, just anyone off the street

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, רבי אמי allowed completing the missing witness on a גט even with a slave from the market.

phrases.english: When they came before Rabbi Ami
he said to him
Go out and complete it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the גט that was missing a witness.

phrases.english: with a slave from the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling for the missing-witness topic discussed in the earlier steps.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גט missing a witness may be completed even with a slave from the marketplace.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הזורק
steps.stepSummary: The formal closing line for the chapter הזורק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הזורק.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter called הזורק. A new chapter starts right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a closing formula said at the end of every chapter. It is not part of the legal argument. It just tells us one chapter is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the chapter-closing formula)
The name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaZorek.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter whose last ruling was just given.

steps.title: A גט with an exception: רבי אליעזר permits, חכמים forbid
steps.stepSummary: A new chapter opens. A husband divorces his wife but says she may marry anyone except one man, and רבי אליעזר and חכמים disagree about whether this works.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who divorces his wife and says to her: 'You are hereby permitted to any man, except so-and-so.' רבי אליעזר permits, and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter's משנה presents a case: the husband gives a גט but leaves out one man she may not marry. רבי אליעזר says the divorce works, and חכמים say it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט frees the woman to marry anyone. Here the husband holds back one person. The argument is whether a divorce that does not free her completely still counts as a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: One who divorces; also the name of the new chapter
Permitted to (marry) any man; the key wording of a גט
Except for so-and-so
The תנא who says the גט is valid here
The Sages, who say she remains forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forbid' here means the חכמים do not let her marry anyone through this גט, because to them the divorce did not work at all. It does not just mean she can't marry the one man who was left out.

phrases.english: One who divorces his wife
and said to her
"You are hereby permitted to any man
except for so-and-so"
Rabbi Eliezer permits
and the Sages forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new chapter and topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט given with 'permitted to any man except so-and-so': רבי אליעזר says it is valid; חכמים say it is not.

steps.title: How to fix the גט: give it again without the exception
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what the husband should do: take the גט back and give it again, this time freeing her to marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should he do? He takes it from her, gives it to her again, and says to her: 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a practical fix, so that the divorce works even according to חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was the spoken exception, not the גט paper itself. So the same גט can be handed over again, this time with a full release and no man left out.

keyTerms.meaning: What should he do? (asking for the practical fix)
He should take it (back)
And give it again

phrases.english: What should he do?
He should take it from her
and give it to her again
and say to her
"You are hereby permitted to any man."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical fix for the problem raised by the חכמים in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To fix the divorce, the husband takes the גט back and gives it again with a full release.

steps.title: An exception written inside the גט ruins it, even if erased
steps.stepSummary: If the husband wrote the exception into the גט itself, the גט is invalid, even if he later erased the words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote it inside it, even though he then erased it, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a stricter case: the exception was not just spoken but actually written in the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the paper itself was written in a bad way. Erasing the words afterward does not help, because the גט was not written properly to begin with. So the fix from step 10 does not work, and a new גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He wrote it (the exception) inside it (the גט)
He erased it
Invalid

steps.whatToRemember: A spoken exception can be fixed by giving the גט again. A written exception makes the גט invalid, even after erasing it.

phrases.english: If he wrote it inside it
phrases.notes: He wrote the 'except so-and-so' words right into the גט itself.

phrases.english: even though he then erased it
it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתָבוֹ בְּתוֹכוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָזַר וּמְחָקוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the fix of step 10: it only works when the exception was spoken, not written.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An exception written into the גט makes it invalid even if erased.

steps.title: Does אלא mean 'excluding' or 'on condition'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the husband's word אלא means: an exclusion from the divorce, or a condition attached to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was raised: this word אלא — does it mean 'excluding,' or does it mean 'on condition'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking how to understand the word אלא. This sets up the next steps, which will show how the answer changes the argument between רבי אליעזר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלא means חוץ ('excluding'), the husband is cutting one man out of the divorce itself, so the divorce is not complete. If it means על מנת ('on condition'), he gives a full divorce with a condition attached, like any regular condition. The גמרא wants to know which reading the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (an open question)
Excluding; leaving something out
On condition that

steps.confusionAlert: This is a real question, not an attack on the משנה. The גמרא is trying to understand what the husband's words mean. Step 17 gives the answer.

phrases.english: Gemara
A question was raised before them
this word "ella"
does it mean "excluding"
or does it mean "on condition"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הַאי ״אֶלָּא״ – ״חוּץ״ הוּא, אוֹ ״עַל מְנָת״ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's key word in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the husband's אלא means an exclusion from the divorce (חוץ) or a condition attached to it (על מנת).

steps.title: First option: אלא means 'except'
steps.stepSummary: If אלא means 'except' (חוץ), then the חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר over 'except'. They agree with him about a condition, which works like any normal condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it mean 'except'? If so, the רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר about 'except', because the husband left part of her freedom out of the גט. But with 'on condition' they agree with him, just like all ordinary conditions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first side of the question it asked in step 12. It shows how the מחלוקת would look if אלא means 'except'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, 'except' is the problem case. The husband held back part of the woman's freedom, so the חכמים say the גט fails. A condition, though, is just like any other תנאי, so everyone agrees the גט works.

keyTerms.meaning: Except: an exclusion carved out of the divorce itself
On condition: a תנאי attached to the divorce
He left something over in the גט, so it does not fully cut the tie
Ordinary conditions that apply everywhere

phrases.english: Is it "except"?
Then it is about "except" that they disagree:
the Rabbis against Rabbi Eliezer,
since he left something over for her in the גט;
phrases.notes: He kept one man off-limits, so the גט doesn't fully free her.

phrases.english: but with "on condition" they agree with him,
just as with all ordinary conditions;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the question from step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אלא means 'except', which would place the מחלוקת on exclusions while everyone accepts conditions.

steps.title: Second option: אלא means 'on condition'
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps אלא means 'on condition'. Then רבי אליעזר argues with the חכמים over a condition. He agrees with them that 'except' fails, because the husband left something over in the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it means 'on condition'. Then it is about 'on condition' that רבי אליעזר argues with the רבנן. But with 'except' he concedes the גט is invalid, since the husband left something over in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Here the מחלוקת is about a condition, and everyone agrees that 'except' does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides flip which case is in dispute. In this version, the case everyone agrees on is the 'except' case, and they agree it fails. רבי אליעזר's lenient view applies only to a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: introduces the second side of a question
He agrees (concedes)

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is "on condition";
then it is about "on condition" that he disagrees:
Rabbi Eliezer against the Rabbis;
but with "except" he agrees
that it fails, since he left something over for her in the גט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question, the opposite of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אלא means 'on condition', which would place the מחלוקת on conditions while everyone agrees that exclusions fail.

steps.title: רבינא's proof from houses with נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a משנה: all houses get טומאה from נגעים, אלא those of gentiles. Reading אלא as 'on condition' gives a ridiculous meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come hear. 'All houses become impure through נגעים, אלא those of gentiles.' If אלא means 'except', the line reads well. But if it means 'on condition', the line would say: Jewish houses become impure on condition that gentile houses don't. So if gentile houses did become impure, Jewish houses would not?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries to answer the question using another משנה that uses the same word אלא. He shows that only 'except' makes sense there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the נגעים משנה, 'except' simply leaves gentile houses out of the rule. Reading it as 'on condition' would make Jewish houses' טומאה depend on what happens to gentile houses, which is absurd. So the word אלא in a משנה must mean 'except'.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a proof from a source
Leprous marks (צרעת) that can make a house טמא
Granted: this option works fine
Fine, it reads well

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
All houses become impure through leprous marks,
"ella" those of gentiles.
Granted, if you say it means "except," it reads well;
but if you say it means "on condition,"

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת דְּלָא מִיטַּמּוּ בָּתֵּי גוֹיִם
phrases.english: then it is on condition that gentile houses do not become impure
that Jewish houses become impure,
so if gentile houses do become impure,
Jewish houses would not become impure?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from steps 13 and 14.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in נגעים: all houses become impure through נגעים except those of gentiles.

steps.title: Second point: gentile houses never become impure
steps.stepSummary: A second argument: gentile houses cannot get נגעים at all, as a ברייתא learns from a פסוק. So a 'condition' about their טומאה would be meaningless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Moreover, do gentile houses become impure at all? A ברייתא teaches: 'And I put a plague of צרעת in a house of the land of your possession.' The land of your possession becomes impure through נגעים, but gentile houses do not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why 'on condition' cannot be right in the נגעים משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gentile houses can never become impure, according to the פסוק. So a condition that 'gentile houses don't become impure' would always be met and would mean nothing. The only sensible reading is that the משנה is leaving gentile houses out of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Moreover: adds another argument
But it was taught in a ברייתא
The land of your possession, meaning land owned by Jews

phrases.english: And moreover, do gentile houses become impure at all?!
But it was taught:
"And I put a plague of leprosy
in a house of the land of your possession"
the land of your possession becomes impure through leprous marks,
but gentile houses do not become impure through leprous marks!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבינא's proof with a second argument.
steps.raayaObject: That 'on condition' cannot be the meaning of אלא in the נגעים משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 14:34 teaching that gentile houses do not get נגעים.

steps.title: Conclusion: אלא means 'except'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that אלא means 'except' (חוץ).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that it means 'except.' Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבינא's proof and settles the question: אלא means 'except'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question from step 12. Going back to step 13, it means the חכמים argue with רבי אליעזר over 'except', the case where the husband left something over in the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: אלא in our משנה means חוץ, 'except'. So the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים is about a גט that carves out one man.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this that it means "except";
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבינא's proof and settles the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אלא means 'except', so the משנה's מחלוקת concerns a גט that excludes one man.

steps.title: A ברייתא where everyone agrees 'except' fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that our משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He holds that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים agree that a גט saying 'permitted to everyone except so-and-so' does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים did not argue about a man who divorces his wife and tells her, 'You are permitted to any man except so-and-so.' Everyone agrees she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know our משנה is about 'except,' the גמרא points out a תנא who sees the argument differently. It starts quoting his ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about 'except.' רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says there is no argument there at all, and both sides agree the woman is not divorced. So he must place the argument somewhere else, and the next step shows where.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A sage of the משנה period whose teaching is quoted
As it is taught in a ברייתא
They did not disagree
So-and-so, a specific person left unnamed
Divorced

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this ברייתא proves רבי אליעזר wrong. It only says that a different תנא remembers the argument as being about a different case than our משנה does.

phrases.english: Our משנה is not in line with this tanna
phrases.notes: Step 17 showed our משנה has them arguing over 'except.' This תנא says nobody argues about that.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:
Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis did not disagree
about one who divorces his wife

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לָהּ: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם,
phrases.english: and says to her: 'You are hereby permitted to any man,
except for so-and-so'
that she is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that אלא means 'except' and shows a תנא who disagrees with our משנה's version of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, everyone agrees that a גט saying 'except so-and-so' does not divorce the woman.

steps.title: The real argument is about a condition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים do argue: a man who says 'you are permitted to anyone, on condition that you do not marry so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they argue? About a man who divorces his wife and tells her, 'You are permitted to any man, on condition that you do not marry so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks where the argument actually is and names the case. It is setting up the ruling, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא moves the argument from 'except' to 'on condition.' This is the opposite of our משנה. In our משנה, as step 17 concluded, the argument is about 'except,' and both sides agree a condition works.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they disagree?
On condition that
You will marry

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows there are two versions of the argument between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים. One is about 'except' and the other is about a condition.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About one who divorces his wife

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לָהּ: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם,
phrases.english: and says to her: 'You are hereby permitted to any man,
on condition that you do not marry so-and-so'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 18 by naming the case the two sides actually argue about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the argument is about a גט given 'on condition that you do not marry so-and-so.'
